findings.reason: the plan should route the demonstration scorer onto the existing referee's scorecard so both EFIT-X definitions stay one definition, which removes a second reader rather than adding one.
findings.text: the scorer takes the saddle-to-EFIT-X and LCFS distances from hardcoded per-machine bank keys (`binding_to_efit_lcfs_rms_m`, `selected_saddle_to_efit_x_point_m`; DIII-D `closed_boundary_symmetric_rms_distance_m`, `polished_saddle_to_nearest_efit_x_m`) instead of the existing EFIT-parity comparator `nova/imas/mast_efit_referee.py:compare_reference_geometry` (:129–:140), which already emits `X_POINT_DISTANCE_M`, `LCFS_DISTANCE_M` and `TOPOLOGY_CLASS_AGREEMENT_FRACTION` from the same `efm` reads — a second EFIT-geometry reader will drift from the referee's definition

findings.reason: the receipt already carries the thresholds verbatim and the plan's decision text is the authoritative preregistration, so moving the constants into the registry is tidiness, not a correction to the design.
findings.text: the three locked demonstration thresholds (class agreement 7/12, closed-boundary RMS 0.55 m, saddle 0.04 m) live as module constants in the benchmark script rather than extending the pre-registered tolerance registry (`MetricTolerance`, `parity_tolerances.py:94`) that owns every other pre-registered bound

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the extraction thrust hides curve generation, stationary polish and branch identity behind `traced_spline_contour` + `separatrix_branches` + `boundary_comparison.compare_closed_boundaries`; the comparison is one fail-closed function, so the behaviour hidden exceeds the interface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the demonstration gate re-reads EFIT geometry through bespoke per-bank JSON field names rather than the existing EFIT referee that owns those same reads.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design is backed by a 25-candidate reuse map (docs/figures/efit-baseline-demonstration/reuse-map.md) naming `traced_spline_contour`, `stencil_nulls.xpoint_candidates`, `separatrix_clip._traced_clip`, the MAST referee and the DIII-D harness, and it reduces the new surface to one missing contract (the closed/open branch assembler now in nova/equilibrium/separatrix_branches.py).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — nova/equilibrium/boundary_comparison.py is a small host-only layer, but the reuse map justifies it explicitly ("their boundary metrics need one common closed-boundary implementation"), which is the justification the item asks for.
